---
title: "Bugs fixed after ipw 1.3.2"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(ipw)
library(survival)

# Results of ipw 1.2.1.1 and ipw 1.3.2 (CRAN), made once with
# data-raw/make-bugfix-article-data.R. The correct weights and the results of
# the version that builds this page are computed below, every time.
stored <- readRDS("bug-fixes-old-versions.rds")
cases <- stored$cases
data("haartdat", package = "ipw")
cases$ties$data <- haartdat

run_now <- function(cs) {
  warns <- character()
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(eval(cs$call, list(data = cs$data)), error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  err <- inherits(fit, "error")
  list(weights = if (err) NULL else as.numeric(fit$ipw.weights),
       error = if (err) conditionMessage(fit) else NA_character_,
       warnings = unique(warns))
}
now <- lapply(cases, run_now)
this_version <- paste0("this version (", utils::packageVersion("ipw"), ")")

results <- function(nm) {
  r <- list(stored$old[["1.2.1.1"]]$results[[nm]], stored$old[["1.3.2"]]$results[[nm]], now[[nm]])
  names(r) <- c("1.2.1.1", "1.3.2 (CRAN)", this_version)
  r
}
max_rel <- function(w, ref) max(abs(w / ref - 1))
short <- function(x, n = 110) ifelse(nchar(x) > n, paste0(substr(x, 1, n), "..."), x)
describe <- function(x) {
  if (!is.na(x$error)) return(paste("Error:", short(x$error)))
  if (length(x$warnings)) return(paste("Weights, with warning:", short(x$warnings[1])))
  "Weights"
}
version_table <- function(nm, ref = NULL) {
  r <- results(nm)
  tab <- data.frame(
    Version = names(r),
    Result = vapply(r, describe, ""),
    Difference = vapply(r, function(x) {
      if (is.null(ref) || is.null(x$weights)) return("")
      formatC(max_rel(x$weights, ref), format = "g", digits = 2)
    }, ""),
    check.names = FALSE)
  names(tab)[3] <- "Largest relative difference from the correct weights"
  knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

This page describes the bugs that were found in a review of ipw after
version 1.3.2 and fixed in the next version. For each bug it shows a small
example and runs it in three versions:

* **ipw 1.2.1.1**, the last version before the 1.3 rewrite;
* **ipw 1.3.2**, the version on CRAN when the review was done;
* **this version**, the one this page was built with.

The weights of each version are compared with the *correct* weights, which
are computed by hand on this page with `glm()`, `MASS::polr()` or
`survival::coxph()`, without using ipw. A difference of about 1e-15 is
rounding; a difference of 0.1 means that some weights are off by 10%.

The results of 1.2.1.1 and 1.3.2 were made once in separate R sessions with
the script `data-raw/make-bugfix-article-data.R` and are stored with this
article; the correct weights and the results of this version are computed
every time the page is built.

```{r summary, echo = FALSE}
status <- function(x, ref, should_stop = FALSE) {
  if (should_stop) return(if (is.na(x$error)) "wrong (no error)" else "error, as it should")
  if (!is.na(x$error)) return(if (is.null(ref)) "error" else "error (should work)")
  if (is.null(ref)) return("ok")
  d <- max_rel(x$weights, ref)
  if (d < 1e-6) "correct" else sprintf("wrong (up to %s)", formatC(d, format = "g", digits = 2))
}
```

## Who is affected?

You are affected if you used one of the following with an older version. The
sections below explain each case; the table at the end summarises them.

* an `offset()` term in a model formula (1.3.1 and 1.3.2);
* `denominator = ~ .` (1.3.1 and 1.3.2: an error, so no wrong results);
* a 0/1 exposure stored as a factor, with the level `"1"` first (all older
  versions);
* an ordinal exposure stored as text (1.3.1 and 1.3.2; 1.2.1.1 stopped with
  an unclear error), or as a factor whose levels are in alphabetical rather
  than dose order (all older versions);
* `ipwtm()` with `family = "survival"` and `type = "first"` or `"cens"`,
  where subjects have their own visit times (all older versions);
* `ipwtm()` with a covariate that is called `selvar` (1.3.1 and 1.3.2);
* `ipwtm()` with `id`/`timevar` combinations that occur more than once (all
  older versions);
* `ipwtm()` with `family = "survival"` and the `ties` argument (all older
  versions).

## 1. `offset()` terms were dropped (1.3.1 and 1.3.2)

An offset is a term with a fixed coefficient of 1, for example the log of
follow-up time when the chance of exposure grows with time at risk. In ipw
1.3.1 and 1.3.2 the model formula was rebuilt from its term labels, and R
does not count `offset()` as a term label, so the offset was silently left
out: the model was fitted as `a ~ l`.

```{r offset-call}
cases$offset$call
```

The correct weights, by hand:

```{r offset-ref}
d <- cases$offset$data
p <- fitted(glm(a ~ l + offset(off), family = binomial, data = d))
ref_offset <- unname(1 / ifelse(d$a == 1, p, 1 - p))
```

```{r offset-table, echo = FALSE}
version_table("offset", ref_offset)
```

**Fix:** the model formula is now used exactly as written.

## 2. `denominator = ~ .` failed (1.3.1 and 1.3.2)

`~ .` means "all other columns of `data`". In 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 the check for
missing variables looked for a column called `.` and stopped.

```{r dot-call}
cases$dot$call
names(cases$dot$data)
```

```{r dot-ref}
d <- cases$dot$data
p <- fitted(glm(a ~ l1 + l2, family = binomial, data = d))
ref_dot <- unname(1 / ifelse(d$a == 1, p, 1 - p))
```

```{r dot-table, echo = FALSE}
version_table("dot", ref_dot)
```

**Fix:** `~ .` works again in `ipwpoint()`. In `ipwtm()` it is now a clear
error, because the dot would also include the id, time and exposure
columns; list the covariates there.

## 3. A factor exposure with levels `c("1", "0")` swapped the probabilities

For a binomial exposure, ipw checked that the values were 0 and 1, but a
factor with those labels passed the check. `glm()` then models the
probability of the *second* level. With levels in the order `"1"`, `"0"`
that is the probability of being *unexposed*, so every exposed subject got
the weight meant for an unexposed one and vice versa. Factors with levels
`"0"`, `"1"` (the default order) were fine.

```{r factor-call}
cases$factor$call
levels(cases$factor$data$a)
```

```{r factor-ref}
d <- cases$factor$data
p <- fitted(glm(a_num ~ l1 + l2, family = binomial, data = d))
ref_factor <- unname(1 / ifelse(d$a_num == 1, p, 1 - p))
```

```{r factor-table, echo = FALSE}
version_table("factor", ref_factor)
```

**Fix:** a 0/1 exposure stored as a factor or text is converted by its
labels, so the order of the levels no longer matters.

## 4. An ordinal exposure given as text was ordered alphabetically (1.3.1 and 1.3.2)

For `family = "ordinal"` the exposure is turned into a factor. Text is then
sorted alphabetically, so `"low"`, `"mid"`, `"high"` became
`"high" < "low" < "mid"`, and in 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 the ordinal model was
fitted with the wrong order without any message. ipw 1.2.1.1 stopped with an
error that did not say what was wrong. The same alphabetical order is used
in every version for an *unordered factor* with text levels, unless its
levels were set in dose order.

```{r ordinal-call}
cases$ordinal$call
table(cases$ordinal$data$dose)
```

The correct weights use the dose order:

```{r ordinal-ref}
d <- cases$ordinal$data
d$dose_ord <- factor(d$dose, levels = c("low", "mid", "high"), ordered = TRUE)
fit <- MASS::polr(dose_ord ~ l, data = d, method = "logistic")
pr <- predict(fit, type = "probs")
ref_ordinal <- unname(1 / pr[cbind(seq_len(nrow(d)), as.integer(d$dose_ord))])
```

```{r ordinal-table, echo = FALSE}
version_table("ordinal", ref_ordinal)
```

**Fix:** a text exposure is now an error that asks for an ordered factor or
numeric codes, and an unordered factor whose levels are not numbers gives a
warning. With an ordered factor the weights are correct in all versions:

```{r ordinal-ok}
w <- ipwpoint(exposure = dose_ord, family = "ordinal", link = "logit",
              denominator = ~ l, data = d)
max_rel(w$ipw.weights, ref_ordinal)
```

## 5. Survival exposure: subjects with their own visit times

For `family = "survival"` with `type = "first"` (and the censoring weights
with `type = "cens"`), each row covers an interval `(tstart, timevar]`, and
its probability should use the baseline hazard over that interval. Older
versions used the increase in the baseline hazard since the *previous time
point in the whole data set*. That is the same thing when all subjects are
seen at the same times, as in `haartdat`, but not when they have their own
visit times: the hazard of a row was then only counted from the last visit
of *any* subject, so it was too small.

```{r survival-call}
cases$survival$call
head(cases$survival$data[, c("id", "tstart", "time", "a", "l")], 4)
```

The correct weights use the cumulative baseline hazard *H* at both ends of
each row's interval:

```{r survival-ref}
d <- cases$survival$data
fit <- coxph(Surv(tstart, time, a) ~ l, data = d)
bh <- basehaz(fit, centered = TRUE)
H <- function(t) {
  h <- approx(bh$time, bh$hazard, xout = t, method = "constant", rule = 2)$y
  h[t < min(bh$time)] <- 0
  h
}
haz <- (H(d$time) - H(d$tstart)) * predict(fit, type = "risk")
p_obs <- ifelse(d$a == 1, 1 - exp(-haz), exp(-haz))
ref_survival <- unname(ave(1 / p_obs, d$id, FUN = cumprod))
```

(The package tests also check this against a baseline hazard computed from
the risk sets by hand, without `basehaz()`.)

```{r survival-table, echo = FALSE}
version_table("survival", ref_survival)
```

With a common time grid, as in `haartdat`, nothing changes: all versions
give the same weights.

**Fix:** each row now uses the hazard over its own interval, as
`type = "all"` already did.

## 6. A covariate called `selvar` was overwritten (`ipwtm()`, 1.3.1 and 1.3.2)

From version 1.3.1, `ipwtm()` adds a column called `selvar` to the data to
mark the rows that enter the exposure model. A covariate of the user with
that name was overwritten, so the model used the indicator instead.

```{r selvar-call}
cases$selvar$call
```

By hand: the rows up to and including the first exposure enter the model,
and the weights are cumulative products within subject.

```{r selvar-ref}
d <- cases$selvar$data
sel <- ave(d$a, d$id, FUN = function(x) cumsum(cumsum(x)) <= 1) == 1
p <- rep(1, nrow(d))
p[sel] <- fitted(glm(a ~ l + selvar, family = binomial, data = d[sel, ]))
p_obs <- ifelse(!sel, 1, ifelse(d$a == 1, p, 1 - p))
ref_selvar <- unname(ave(1 / p_obs, d$id, FUN = cumprod))
```

```{r selvar-table, echo = FALSE}
version_table("selvar", ref_selvar)
```

**Fix:** the internal column now has a name that does not clash
(`.ipw_selvar`); the `selvar` element of the result is unchanged.

## 7. Duplicated `id`/`timevar` rows were accepted (`ipwtm()`)

If the same subject and time occur twice, for example after a faulty merge,
the cumulative product is taken over both copies in an arbitrary order and
the weights are wrong. `ipwtm()` accepted such data without a message
(`ipwprobtm()` already refused it).

```{r dup-show}
d <- cases$duplicates$data
sum(duplicated(d[, c("id", "time")]))
```

```{r dup-table, echo = FALSE}
version_table("duplicates")
```

**Fix:** duplicated `id`/`timevar` combinations are now an error.

## 8. The `ties` argument was ignored (`ipwtm()`, survival)

Arguments in `...` are passed to the model function. For `family = "survival"`
the Cox model always used Efron's method for tied times, so
`ties = "breslow"` had no effect, in 1.2.1.1 as well as in 1.3.x.

```{r ties-call}
cases$ties$call
```

By hand, with Breslow's method for both models:

```{r ties-ref}
d <- haartdat
sel <- ave(d$haartind, d$patient, FUN = function(x) cumsum(cumsum(x)) <= 1) == 1
p_breslow <- function(rhs) {
  f <- update(rhs, Surv(tstart, fuptime, haartind) ~ .)
  fit <- coxph(f, data = d[sel, ], ties = "breslow")
  bh <- basehaz(fit, centered = TRUE)
  H <- function(t) {
    h <- approx(bh$time, bh$hazard, xout = t, method = "constant", rule = 2)$y
    h[t < min(bh$time)] <- 0
    h
  }
  p <- rep(1, nrow(d))
  haz <- (H(d$fuptime[sel]) - H(d$tstart[sel])) * predict(fit, type = "risk")
  p[sel] <- ifelse(d$haartind[sel] == 1, 1 - exp(-haz), exp(-haz))
  p
}
ref_ties <- unname(ave(p_breslow(~ sex + age) / p_breslow(~ sex + age + cd4.sqrt),
                       d$patient, FUN = cumprod))
```

```{r ties-table, echo = FALSE}
version_table("ties", ref_ties)
```

**Fix:** `ties` is passed on to `coxph()`; the default is still Efron.

## Summary

```{r summary-table, echo = FALSE}
refs <- list(offset = ref_offset, dot = ref_dot, factor = ref_factor,
             ordinal = ref_ordinal, survival = ref_survival, selvar = ref_selvar,
             duplicates = NULL, ties = ref_ties)
labels <- c(offset = "1. offset() in a formula", dot = "2. denominator = ~ .",
            factor = "3. factor exposure, levels \"1\", \"0\"",
            ordinal = "4. ordinal exposure as text",
            survival = "5. survival, own visit times",
            selvar = "6. covariate called selvar",
            duplicates = "7. duplicated id/timevar rows",
            ties = "8. ties = \"breslow\"")
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(labels), function(nm) {
  r <- results(nm)
  st <- vapply(r, status, "", ref = refs[[nm]], should_stop = nm == "duplicates")
  # a text exposure is refused on purpose in this version; 1.2.1.1 also
  # stopped, but with an unclear message
  if (nm == "ordinal") {
    if (!is.na(r[[1]]$error)) st[1] <- "error (unclear message)"
    if (!is.na(r[[3]]$error)) st[3] <- "error, as it should"
  }
  data.frame(Case = labels[[nm]], t(st), check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

All fixes are listed in the [NEWS](../news/index.html). The package tests
(`tests/testthat/test-audit*.R`, `test-regression*.R`) check each case, and
`test-regression.R` checks that, apart from these fixes, the weights are the
same as in ipw 1.2.1.1 for 44 settings.
